verdictOnCurrentFilms: These are slideshows in a dark box. The camera never moves: the same frame repeats nine seconds later in Ford 2/3 and 5/6, Persia 4/5 and Douglass 5/6, so the film holds still for 18+ seconds at a stretch and the only motion is a fade (Douglass 2 to 3 dims to near black). The hero print fills roughly 13 percent of the frame and floats at the top; the lower half is a rounded black caption slab that actually overlaps the picture (it clips the bottom of the Persia seal and the Douglass engraving). The backdrop is a blurred enlargement of each image, so the light wanders amber, black, grey, mustard for no reason and no source: there is no lamp, no surface, no place. There is no title, no chapter, no map, no number on screen, even though Ford's best beat, a chassis built in twelve and a half hours then ninety-three minutes, is just a sentence in a box. Reconstruction is flagged only in a 9px credit at top right, so the painting reads as the evidence. All three films share one font, one amber-brown mood and one layout: no Anton and red-orange for Ford, no wood type and iron-gall gold for Douglass, no lapis and no Syriac or Chinese script for Persia. They do not match their exhibits at all. What is right and must survive: the real photographs are large, centred and unretouched, the Highland Park line frame is a genuine gift, and the faceless paintings (boy at the bench, back-turned driver, empty bishops' hall, stele court) are the honest ones.
concept: THE LIT TABLE. Every film is one continuous shot of one physical table seen by one camera. Same rig, same 35mm-equivalent lens, same move vocabulary (push, truck, rack, pull-back) in all four films, so they read as one family. What changes per exhibit is the table's MATERIAL and its single practical LIGHT: Ford is riveted iron plate under a hanging shop lamp; Douglass is a composing stone and forme under a gas lamp; Persia is rag paper and rubbing ink under a raking shaft of low sun through a slot; Partition is a soot-black map table with one madder-red thread. Archive photographs are physical prints placed on the table at true proportion, always fully and evenly lit across the image area (no vignette, no grade, no tint, no depth-map warping), because light falls off on the surround, never on the evidence. Reconstructions sit on a different z-plane: farther back, smaller, framed, with a RECONSTRUCTION plate on the frame that stays for the whole shot. The drama is the camera's reason for moving (it always arrives at the thing the narrator is about to name, 12 frames before the word) and the beat before the reveal. Depth is a grammar for evidence versus imagination, not a screensaver.
titleSequence: About 8 seconds (192 frames at 24fps), skippable in the player. Black, room tone only for 1 s. The practical lamp swells to 40 percent over 20 frames and the camera starts a slow 6 percent push through the title, which is built as real objects at three depths so the push produces true parallax and raking light reveals them: Ford = the word FORD cut as stencil gaps in an iron plate, signal red-orange #ff4b1f visible only as light leaking through the cuts, set in Anton, 210px cap height; Douglass = DOUGLASS in extruded Abril Fatface wood-type letters, gold #d9b36a catching a hard edge-light, ink-black ground with iron-gall brown-black stone showing; Persia = Cormorant Garamond title with a huge faded Syriac word (church) and the Chinese stele title 大秦景教流行中國碑 carved in the plaster wall BEHIND the English at the far z-plane, lapis #4f7cff light across them, the English never overlapping the script; Partition = FRAUNCES title with the same title in Urdu (Nastaliq), Hindi, Punjabi (Gurmukhi) and English stacked as four lines on the soot map, each language the same cap size and weight, and one madder-red thread #e8553d drawn left to right under them across 36 frames. Years and a one-line honest subtitle (for example 'Told with archive photographs. Paintings are marked Reconstruction.') set in the caption face. The title never reveals word by word and has no counter. End of title: Lamp Dip into the first print.
typography: Display per exhibit (these are the identity): Ford Anton caps, 160-210px titles, 120px chapter cards, stencil gaps in plates, tabular figures for numbers; Douglass Abril Fatface for titles and chapter cards (150-190px) plus a handbill slab for numerals and kickers, set in lead-style slightly irregular ink with 1-2px squash; Persia Cormorant Garamond Light/Italic 120-170px titles with real Syriac (Noto Sans Syriac Estrangela) and Chinese (Noto Serif SC) at 400-520px, 8-12 percent opacity, set deep behind and legible when the camera pushes, proofed by a native reader before render; Partition Fraunces (opsz 144, soft 100) 130-170px, multilingual stacks with Noto Nastaliq Urdu, Noto Serif Devanagari, Noto Sans Gurmukhi at matched optical size. Shared body voice across all four: Source Serif 4 for captions (semibold, 44px at 1080p, 56-char line, max 2 lines), Inter Tight for system labels (RECONSTRUCTION, credit, year) at 26-30px. No tiny tracked gold caps, no ghost numerals under titles, no letterspaced gimmicks; RECONSTRUCTION is the only tracked caps in the film. All type is rendered by the browser (HarfBuzz) so Syriac, Urdu and Devanagari shape correctly; never rasterised in Pillow or set in a video editor.
captionsAndLowerThirds: Kill the black rounded slab. Captions are set on the table surface below the print in the exhibit's own surface colour logic (cream ink on iron/soot, dark ink on rag paper), 44px Source Serif 4, centred, max 2 lines, with a soft 6px shadow only for legibility, never a box. Word-level timing from the narration timing file lights the spoken word to 100 percent while the rest rests at 78 percent. Each caption lives clear of the print; it never overlaps the image. Lower third = the 'slate': a single line (place, year, credit) in Inter Tight 28px that slides out from under the print edge on arrival, holds 4 s, then settles to a 20px credit under the print's corner for the rest of the shot, so credit is always legible and never on the pixels of the photograph. Reconstructions carry a physical RECONSTRUCTION plate on their frame (red-orange stamp for Ford, gold slug for Douglass, lapis tab for Persia, madder tab for Partition), present from first frame to last, plus a one-line note on what it rests on ('Composition imagined; the line itself is documented at left'). Archive photographs get a plain ARCHIVE credit and no label shouting. Gated material: a pre-roll card in the caption voice, then Dead Air, and the image only appears blurred until the viewer has opted in in the player, never auto.
transitions: 1. TABLE TRUCK: within a chapter the camera trucks laterally along the table to the next print, 22 frames, ease-in-out (cubic), landing 12 frames before the next narration phrase. The surround motion-blurs; the prints stay sharp. 2. LAMP DIP: at era changes (year change in the narration) the lamp falls to 12 percent in 10 frames, 6 frames of near black, new set rises in 14 frames with the push already running; the one gesture reserved for chapter breaks. 3. REVEAL UNDER: when a reconstruction is followed by its source, the painting lifts on z, dollies back 8 percent and tilts away to show the archive print or document it rests on, 30 frames; used wherever the narration says 'we know' after 'imagine'. 4. MATCH-EDGE CUT: a hard cut on a narration consonant, matching shape or edge to the same screen position (a line of the line to a line of text); zero frames; used for facts and numbers. 5. SIGNATURE WIPE (one per exhibit): Ford = a stencilled plate slams across in 3 frames with a 2-frame impact shake, on number beats only; Douglass = the forme is inked and a sheet pulled away, 18 frames, on publication/print beats; Persia = a continuous ROAD DOLLY along a long strip composite of places, 3-5 s, no dissolve; Partition = the madder-red line draws across the frame and the cut happens along it, 20 frames. 6. RACK FOCUS: from a near object (a lamp, a pin, a bolt) to the print behind it, 16 frames, used to open a chapter; the print is never softened, only what is in front of it. 7. DEAD AIR: 36 frames of black with real room tone, no music, immediately before the hardest facts (slavery's violence, the martyrs, Partition's killing). No spotlight, no drama: the pause is the honesty. 8. SLOW PULL-BACK on the final image revealing the whole table with every print used, 6 s, into the credits.
motionGraphics: Every graphic is a table object, drawn by the same camera, never a floating overlay. FORD: a stencilled bar 'Chassis build time' shrinks from 12.5 hours to 93 minutes over 2.4 s synced to the line 'twelve and a half hours ... ninety-three minutes', digits ticking in Anton tabular; 15 million Model Ts as a 1,500-dot grid (1 dot = 10,000 cars) filling row by row over 3 s, camera pulling back as it fills; Five Dollar Day as two stencil bars (about $2.34 versus $5.00, verify against source). DOUGLASS: the composing stick sets 'c. 1818' and the last digit stays a blank quad, because he never knew his birthday (unknowing as a typographic event); a thin gold route line from Baltimore to New York, September 1838, on a plain schematic, drawn in 40 frames; the 1845 Narrative title page is the real archive print, camera pushes 8 percent to the imprint line. PERSIA: the road, one lapis line crossing a plain parchment map from Parthia and Mesopotamia to Seleucia-Ctesiphon (410) to Chang'an (635, 781), dots lit as the narrator names each, the Syriac word for 'church' and the Chinese stele title passing behind as the camera travels; the 40 bishops as 40 dots in the hall. PARTITION: the Radcliffe Line drawn as one madder-red thread with a visible ragged width at the district scale; displacement as a stated range ('10 to 20 million people', never a false single number) rendered as a column of small figures-as-dots that spill across the line; the borders it cut set in the four scripts. No numbers appear without a source line and the narration must say them first.

perExhibit.douglass: Composing stone, gas lamp, gold #d9b36a on iron-gall brown-black. Camera low and slow like a press-room dolly. The daguerreotype and the engraving sit as prints on the stone with the real oval, mat and plate edges shown; the Narrative title page lies flat as a printed sheet. The boy-learning-letters beat is carried by the faceless painting only on a back plane with its RECONSTRUCTION slug; no painted Douglass face. Hero gesture: the forme being locked up while he escapes (type locks, then the image of the 1845 page is pulled). Distressing material gated.
perExhibit.ford: Riveted iron plate, hanging shop lamp, red-orange #ff4b1f stencil. Anton titles, parts-bin tags as slate labels. Spine of the film is the Highland Park photograph: a 14 s slow truck along its full width, the only slow-reveal in the film. Back-turned Quadricycle painting and the boy at the bench are allowed on the rear plane, labelled. Ford as a real photograph only, never a painted hero. The 12.5 hours to 93 minutes bar is the film's one big graphic and gets the stencil slam transition.
perExhibit.persia: Rag paper and rubbing ink, a raking slot of low sun, lapis #4f7cff on midnight. The film travels: a single road dolly threads the prints (Syriac gospel reconstruction, the Ctesiphon vault, the bishops' hall, the British Museum seal, the Xi'an Stele court), with the real Syriac and Chinese script carved in the wall behind each, large and slightly out of focus until the camera lands. Keep the seal as a real photograph, big, not clipped by captions. All painted rooms are places or objects only, never people. Dead Air before the martyrdom beat.
perExhibit.partition: Soot-black map table, a single madder-red #e8553d thread, Fraunces with the four-script titles. Archive photographs of 1947 sit as prints, ungraded, nothing animated on their pixels. The thread is the film's only moving colour: drawn at the opening, cutting the map in the middle, and slowly lifted at the end leaving its crease in the paper. Gated material for violence and mass displacement, Dead Air before it, and no painted people in the film at all.

soundTies: Everything is conducted by the narration word-timing file. Cuts and wipes land on a consonant or breath, never on a beat of the music; camera moves start 12 frames before the key word and arrive on it. Captions light word by word from the same timing. The lamp breathes at no more than 3 percent intensity with the score's sustained pedal tone, so light and sound share a pulse nobody consciously notices. SFX are physical and sparse: Ford stencil slam and time-clock tick on number beats, Douglass type-in-stick clicks and press pull, Persia a distant bell and wind through the slot, Partition paper and thread. Score ducks 6 dB under narration, 10 dB under figures. Dead Air carries real room tone, never digital silence. Credits get 3 s of score alone.
productionMethod: Playwright renders a real Three.js/WebGL scene frame by frame at 1920x1080, 24fps (4K only if a master is wanted): perspective camera on a keyframed rig, table material plates (iron, composing stone, rag paper, soot) built procedurally and with scanned textures, prints as flat textured planes at true aspect and with true edges, one physical light with soft shadows on the surround only, shallow depth-of-field applied to the surround and foreground objects but never to the print plane. Type is DOM-rendered (HarfBuzz shaping for Syriac, Nastaliq, Devanagari, Gurmukhi) and sampled as textures so it sits in 3D. Data graphics (bars, dot grids, route lines) are drawn in SVG/canvas inside the same scene and driven by the timing JSON; Lottie is used only for the stamp/label elements that Fabula and Tela also need to reuse. Pillow only for scanning prints to true crop and building plates; ffmpeg encodes (ProRes mezzanine, H.264 CRF 16 delivery, burned-in captions plus separate VTT). Fabula assembles the narration and score and conforms the transition list. Magnific: no credits spent on archive; at most relighting-free texture plates and one or two reconstruction repaints for faceless scenes, never video generation of people, never depth-map parallax on archive images.
risk: A 3D table can read as a diorama gimmick and compete with the evidence, and rendered type in WebGL can mis-shape Syriac or Nastaliq; render time scales with DOF. Mitigations: one rig, rigid camera moves only, light on the surround not the print, a Syriac/Urdu shaping test before any render, and a still-frame review of every print against its source scan for pixel fidelity (no tint, no vignette, no warp). If the owner wants more spectacle than evidence allows, the honest answer is more camera and more silence, not more effects.

arguesWith.why: GENERATIVE will want to animate the paintings and archive stills into moving shots and add depth-map parallax to faces because it looks premium. I say no: it fabricates motion and geometry on evidence, and the honest cinematic move is a real-camera-style push on a flat print. Spend generative budget on material plates and faceless reconstructions, and let the camera, light and silence do the drama.
